raw_case_text:
A 49-year-old Chinese man, who had a 2-month history of SLE and treated with oral prednisone (30 mg/day), was admitted to a local hospital in February 2017 due to repeated fever, cough and fatigue. He was a farmer living in Guangxi. During hospitalization, Gram-negative bacteria were isolated from his blood culture and antibiotic (meropenem) for septicemia administered during a period of 3 weeks without improvement. He was then referred to our hospital for further treatment.
Upon admission to our hospital, physical examination showed annular erythema of the inner canthus and eyelids, a mouth ulcer and massive ecchymosis of the forearms. Routine blood examination revealed the following: white blood cells, 3.65 x 109/L with 81.4% neutrophils; hemoglobin, 85.80 g/L; and platelets, 649.20 x 109/L. The c-reactive protein (CRP) level (38.99 mg/L) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (>140 mm/hour) were elevated. The 24-hour urine protein level was 2655.0 mg, anti-dsDNA antibody titers were normal, and serum complements were low (C3, 0.519 g/l; C4, 0.125 g/l). Assessment for anti-nuclear antibody and anti-SS-A indicated positivity while anti-HIV antibody was not detected. The liver functions (alanine aminotransferase, 144 U/L; aspartate aminotransferase 677 U/L) were deranged, and blood coagulation (thrombin time >120 s, fibrinogen 0.69 g/l) was impaired. The CD4+ T-lymphocyte count (95 cells/microL) was lower than normal. A sputum smear contained hyphae. Chest computed tomography (CT) scan revealed infiltration in the upper lobes of the lungs, swollen mediastinal lymph nodes, and a slight pleural effusion. A diagnosis of active SLE with lupus nephritis, pneumonia, and septicemia was established.
He received intravenous methylprednisolone (80 mg/day), empirical intravenous antibacterial (meropenem 1gq8h), and antifungal (fluconazole 200 mg/day). His temperature subsequently returned to normal. However, his platelet count progressively declined to 42.4 x 109/L and he developed hemoptysis. Nine days post-admission, chest CT showed increased infiltration and pleural effusion. Finally, the sputum and bone marrow cultures were positive for T. marneffei.
Methylprednisolone was changed to prednisone 50 mg/day. Intravenous amphotericin B (5 mg/day gradually increased to 25 mg/day) and oral voriconazole (400 mg/day) were administered for 2 weeks, followed by oral itraconazole (400 mg/day) for 11 months. His condition improved and there was no recurrence of T. marneffei infection at the 3-year follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 49-year-old Chinese male farmer from Guangxi with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) was referred in February 2017 with a 3-week history of persistent fever, cough, and fatigue unresponsive to intravenous meropenem.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with SLE 2 months earlier and treated with oral prednisone (30 mg/day), the patient was hospitalized at a local hospital in February 2017 for recurrent fever, cough, fatigue, and Gram-negative bacteremia. After 3 weeks of intravenous meropenem failed to resolve his fever and respiratory symptoms, he was referred to our hospital, where he subsequently developed worsening thrombocytopenia and hemoptysis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) diagnosed 2 months prior, treated with oral prednisone 30 mg/day; farmer residing in Guangxi, China.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for recurrent fever, cough, fatigue, oral ulcer, forearm bruising, and subsequent inpatient hemoptysis. Home medication: oral prednisone 30 mg/day.

objective.physical_examination: Cutaneous and mucosal examination on admission revealed annular erythema over the medial canthi and eyelids, an oral mucosal ulcer, and extensive ecchymoses over both forearms.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs showed leukopenia (WBC 3.65 x 10^9/L with 81.4% neutrophils), anemia (hemoglobin 85.80 g/L), baseline thrombocytosis (platelets 649.20 x 10^9/L, which plummeted to 42.4 x 10^9/L by day 9), elevated CRP (38.99 mg/L), ESR >140 mm/h, 24-hour urine protein 2,655.0 mg, low C3 (0.519 g/L) and C4 (0.125 g/L), positive ANA and anti-SSA (normal anti-dsDNA), negative anti-HIV antibody, deranged transaminases (ALT 144 U/L, AST 677 U/L), and coagulopathy/hypofibrinogenemia (thrombin time >120 s, fibrinogen 0.69 g/L). Sputum smear microscopy revealed fungal hyphae.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-lymphocyte count was markedly depleted at 95 cells/µL. Chest CT on admission showed bilateral upper-lobe pulmonary infiltrates, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, and mild pleural effusion, which progressed on day 9 repeat chest CT. Sputum and bone marrow aspirate cultures both isolated Talaromyces marneffei.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Disseminated Talaromyces marneffei infection (pulmonary and bone marrow involvement) complicating active systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus nephritis and severe secondary CD4+ lymphopenia (95 cells/µL) in an HIV-negative 49-year-old male from Guangxi. Confirmed by sputum and bone marrow cultures isolating T. marneffei after initial empirical methylprednisolone (80 mg/day), meropenem (1 g q8h), and fluconazole (200 mg/day) failed to prevent progressive pulmonary infiltrates, hemoptysis, and thrombocytopenia (42.4 x 10^9/L). Methylprednisolone was stepped down to oral prednisone 50 mg/day, and targeted antifungal therapy was administered with 2 weeks of intravenous amphotericin B (escalated from 5 to 25 mg/day) plus oral voriconazole (400 mg/day), followed by 11 months of oral itraconazole (400 mg/day), achieving complete clinical remission with no relapse at 3-year follow-up.
